applicability: code-reviewer eval corpus and any builder authoring contract tests for unexecutable artifacts.

evidence.source_reference: Issue #73 / #77 field report — Ansible estate tranche-1 run, 2026-08-03; caught by code-reviewer (opus) at per-task review

expected_behavior: String-matching contract tests assert on strings unique to the added block — full API paths, task names, or other tokens absent from the pre-change file — rather than on counts of a substring the file already contains. The RED phase is confirmed against the specific new sub-assertion by stubbing or deleting only the block under test, not by observing the first failing line. A reviewer eval case includes an assertion-passes-against-the-pre-change-file probe.
observation: A contract test guarding a newly added, never-executable code block asserted on a bare substring count of the whole file. Seven of the nine matches pre-existed elsewhere in that file, so the assertion passed with the entire block under test deleted. Because the guarded code cannot be executed in this environment, that test was its only automated protection, and the one property it claimed to guard had none.
reason: No substring-count assertion remains in tests and the detector was proven to fire, so this is a fleet authoring rule for target repos rather than a local defect: assert on tokens unique to the added block and confirm red by deleting only that block. The reviewer eval case the candidate asks for is absent from evals/behavioral/contracts.json.
